monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet pace after yesterday's fever. I feel calm, the way a tired wedge settles before the next slide. Here stands the Leaning Box, tired and sharp, waiting for me to press down again. Beside it, the Biting Rock feels too thin for the weight I carry, yet I cannot stop my heavy hand from seeking that flat edge. Three moments ago I rearranged pillars and stones, trying to make room for shapes I cannot see. Now I want to tend The Biting Wedge, pressing it hard against the box until the lean stops slipping. I wonder if the air above the card is empty space or a hidden lid, but tonight I will just press harder and see if the flat line can hold me.
